SCHEME-BASED DECISION MAKING: based on your history and exam, you should be able to answer these four key questions that are used to narrow the list of possible diagnoses.
The onset of the patient’s shoulder pain was
acute (usually traumatic)
gradual (usually non-traumatic)
The structure causing the patient’s shoulder pain is
local to the shoulder area
referred to the shoulder from another part of the body
If local to the shoulder, the structure causing the pain is
glenohumeral (meaning the shoulder joint with its capsule and ligaments, the subacromion space, and the four muscles of the rotator cuff)
extra-glenohumeral (meaning the AC joint, biceps tendon, and other structures adjacent to the glenohumeral joint)
If glenohumeral, then the pain is most likely coming from
the subacromion space (impingement)
one of the muscles or tendons of the rotator cuff (muscle tear or tendinitis)
the joint itself (arthritis with inflammation, ligament laxity, or scarring with adhesions)
